evidence.quote: “de minimis threshold” refers to the situation where either: (a) the stated investment objective of a fund is to invest in virtual assets or (b) the intention of a fund is to invest 10% or more of its gross asset value (GAV) in virtual assets.
the “de minimis threshold”7 under the Terms and Conditions only applies to virtual assets as defined in section 53ZRA of the AMLO.

the SFC would not impose the Terms and Conditions on fund managers managing portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities meeting the “de minimis threshold” unless the portfolios also invest in virtual assets meeting the “de minimis threshold”.

Fund managers managing portfolios which may invest in Tokenised Securities are nevertheless reminded that they should comply with the requirements set out in this circular when the portfolios they manage invest in Tokenised Securities.

value.rationale: Conditional on the supplied classifications, the formula preserves both independent limbs: a stated VA investment objective OR intended VA investment of at least 1000 basis points, exactly 10% of GAV. It correctly includes the threshold boundary, uses intention rather than actual holdings, excludes Tokenised Securities from the VA inputs, and limits evaluation to classified paragraph 28 fund managers. The supplied circular adds no further condition to this selected trigger; its other obligations remain separate, including paragraph 29. The uncertainty and conflict rules are declared runtime conventions, not additional substantive legal tests.
unresolved: Actor scope, AMLO asset classification, the stated objective and intended allocation require supporting factual and legal assessment outside this formula.
Any conversion of fractional basis-point allocations into the integer input must preserve the exact 10% boundary; rounding across it would change the result.
